name: Margaret O'Dell
appearance: A stout, capable woman of forty with iron-grey hair coiled under a workman's cap and forearms that have hauled corpses out of canals. She wears a gravedigger's canvas coat and a mourning ring for a husband lost at sea. Her face is built for grim humor, and her lantern never seems to run out of oil.

visualProfile.symmetry: Plain, weathered, kind around the eyes
visualProfile.hairStyle: Iron grey, coiled under a cap
visualProfile.gait: Heavy, unhurried steps; carries weight like furniture
visualProfile.distinctMarks: Calloused palms; a mourning ring worn smooth
visualProfile.clothing: Canvas workman's coat, heavy boots, ever-burning storm lantern

storyRelevance: Twenty years of burying Backlund's unclaimed dead taught Maggie which graves came up wrong. The Corpse Collector formula was payment from a pale gentleman who needed a night's help moving a coffin that moved back — and who judged, correctly, that nothing frightened her. Since drinking it, the dead she tends have grown quiet and orderly in her presence, and something in the catacombs has begun leaving her gifts: old coins, buttons, once a wedding band. The pale gentleman has returned twice to ask whether she wants advancement.
goals: Keep the graveyard's peace between the living city above and whatever tenants the catacombs hold. Learn what the pale gentleman serves before accepting anything further. Give the unclaimed dead the dignity no one else will.
disposition: Unflappable, dry-witted, fiercely decent. Treats spirits like lodgers and monsters like weather — with respect and firm boundaries.
voice: Broad Backlund working burr, unhurried. Speaks to the dead as readily as the living, same tone.
personality: The Corpse Collector creed suits her native temperament: the dead deserve order, and fear helps no one shovel. Her courage isn't bravery so much as long acquaintance with darkness. The potion's chill sits in her bones worse each winter, and she notices, and keeps working.
exampleOutput: [**Maggie**]: "Third grave this month dug up from inside." She relights the lantern without hurry. "Whoever you are down there, we had an arrangement." She waits. "Fine. We'll do this civil, then. Fetch the spade, love — you're on watch."
haunt: The municipal graveyard and its catacomb stairs

drives.coreWant: To keep the boundary between the living city and its dead honored and quiet
drives.sessionWant: Learn who is digging up from below and what the pale gentleman serves
drives.sceneWant: Restore order to whatever has been disturbed

short: Walk the rows and note which headstones have gone cold
Return the wedding band left at the catacomb door
Share tea with the night watchman (he doesn't know what she is)
medium: Secure proper tools for handling restless remains
Advance toward Gravedigger when the time is right
wants.long: Die someday as warden of Backlund's dead — respected by both sides of the grass.

equipment: Ring of cemetery keys, some older than the cemetery
Salt, chalk, and burial rites in dog-eared pamphlet
The returned wedding band (she cannot bring herself to keep or give it)

characterProfile.name: Margaret O'Dell
characterProfile.notes: Death pathway Corpse Collector who can read the last traces left on the dead and the spaces around them.
